title: Enforcing The Social Safety Net

Enforcing The Social Safety Net

Ernan Cui

Gavekal Dragonomics | 11 Nov 2026

China’s government has long been urged to strengthen its social safety net to alleviate households’ uncertainty about the future, lower their savings rate and thereby unlock stronger consumption. And indeed there has been progress, with the government recently rolling out new social programs, expanding existing ones and promising more funding. The latest Five-Year Plan even enshrines a goal of delivering income growth and a stronger safety net to ensure that “households will have greater financial security, more stable expectations and stronger confidence in consumption.” Today, the various programs that make up China’s social safety net are getting more political attention than in many years.For China’s policymakers, though, the current goal of strengthening the social safety net is mostly about ensuring more of the population is enrolled in official social-insurance programs, rather than increasing benefits or transfers. The heightened focus on coverage has been driven by the spread of informal or “flexible” jobs in which workers rarely pay into the social security system, a trend that raises concerns about both social stability and the financial sustainability of benefits.
